paper_diagnosis: Delayed lower urinary tract symptoms and erectile dysfunction after acute episode of coccidioidal meningitis
disease_label_per_paper: Coccidioidal meningitis with later lower urinary tract and erectile dysfunction complications
presentation_summary: 27-year-old man presented with several weeks of worsening headaches, myalgias, and nausea requiring hospitalization.
Lumbar puncture showed marked CSF pleocytosis greater than 800 x 10^3/mL with 20% eosinophils.
Coccidioides immitis was cultured from CSF; head CT and MRI showed no hydrocephalus or lesions.
He received lipid-complexed amphotericin B plus high-dose fluconazole; amphotericin was stopped because of renal failure, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, and anemia.
Two months after discharge he developed urinary urgency, incontinence, erectile dysfunction, retrograde ejaculation, and decreased penile sensation, despite normal repeat neuroimaging.
